svg.title: Heating & gas pressure
svg.desc: Internal energy: Total kinetic + potential energy of all particles. Temperature is related to average kinetic energy. ΔE = mcΔθ when temperature changes; use kg, J/kg°C and a temperature difference. Latent heat: E = mL, L in J/kg. Change state without changing temperature. Melting/boiling: potential energy rises. Freezing/condensing releases energy. c and L describe different changes. Heating graphs: Slopes: temperature rises. Plateaus: state changes while energy still enters. Constant-power heating: longer time means more input energy. Cooling gives the reverse changes. Combine stages: 0.10 kg ice at 0°C → water at 20°C: mL + mcΔθ. With L = 334,000 and c = 4,200, total = 41,800 J. At 100 W, ideal time = 418 s; losses add time. Fixed-volume heating: Fixed mass: hotter → higher average kinetic energy → faster particles. More frequent wall collisions and larger momentum changes → greater force per area → greater pressure. Volume & compression: Fixed mass, constant T: pV constant. 100 kPa × 60 cm³ = 150 kPa × 40 cm³. Rapid compression does work and may heat gas, so constant-T rule may not apply.
